newsitem.title: UK: German 1996 cocoa grind seen up 3-5 pct - BDS.
newsitem.headline: German 1996 cocoa grind seen up 3-5 pct - BDS.

text.p: The German cocoa grind for all 1996 should come in between three and five percent higher than the year ago, Karsten Keunecke, managing director of the German confectionery industry association BDS said on Friday.
"I believe the fourth quarter will be along the lines of what we have seen so far."
"The overall economy is not good but the chocolate side has been better," he said in comments to a reporter at meetings of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO).
Domestic consumtion was slow but exports to eastern Europe and former Russian republics rose steadily, Keunecke said.
The German grind was up by 0.1 percent in the first quarter of the year, by 5.3 percent in the second quarter and by seven percent in the third quarter compared with year ago periods.
The total grind for the whole of 1995 was 258,817 tonnes.
